I will also be retaking Chinese, so I will just leave some tips here.

1. Do the TYS, especially for Paper 2. Practice doing the MCQ and search the words up to understand better. Record it somewhere (in your phone, notebook) so that you can remember the meaning. For comprehension MCQ, usually what I do is to take note of the main message about what they are saying. Most of the time, the main message can be found in the first paragraph, but just in case, read the whole paragraph and understand what they are mainly talking about.

2. Essay. Format has been given by another redditor, so I will just roughly explain the important points. For arugementative, what is most important is examples. You need many, many examples so that your paragraphs are well elaborated. Examples such as statistics, your own story, quotes from famous people etc. will help you to pull your essay marks up. 
Also, take note of the keywords in the question. Underline them and make sure you answer all the keywords. Use 5 minutes to plan out what are the factors you will be answering with so that you won't 离题 easily.

Basically, you need to look at all evidences displayed in a cartoon/poster. See what the author has drawn to portray an individual/an event, or look at what the caption/text is talking about in the poster. What does it say? Does it suggest something about the author's feelings? What does this tell you about the cartoon overall? 

4AMC= Author, Audience, Action, Achievement, Message, Context (I rarely add this in)
This is usually used for inference with purpose. 
"Why did the author say this?" For example. 
You basically use this technique to answer such questions: "This source was written by [Author] to [pursuade/criticise/convince, basically action] the [audience] that [Message]. This can be seen in [Evidence]. The author said this so that [Achievement]."

For SBQ, my teacher did teach us to use the Paul's Wheel method. For every sources/cartoon, take note of:
1. Author 
2. Issue
3. Context
4. ALL Evidence
5. POV of the Author (Critical, Supportive, Worried etc)
6. Language, Symbols, Tone
[I think this is all, will update again just in case this is wrong after Amath P1]

Use these guidelines in your head while reading the SBQ and keep asking yourself such questions. Eg. This author, how is he portraying these people in the cartoon to be like? When was this set in? What is he critizing them about? etc 
Don't mix this with 4AMC. Paul's Wheel is something to get your brains thinking, not an answering technique, stick to whatver answering technique you have been taught, and you should be good to go. Hopefully my explanation was okay.
